title: Ultrastable de novo SuperMyo proteins enable high-performance macroscopic fibers from minimal repeats

key_results: Tensile strength of 372 MPa and toughness of 61 MJ m⁻³ achieved with tetrameric constructs; unfolding forces nearly double those of natural immunoglobulin domains
comments: The strategy of engineering intrinsic mechanostability rather than chain length is elegant, though scalability of computational design and wet-spinning remains to be demonstrated at industrial scale.

hypotheses.result: Unfolding forces nearly doubled compared to natural immunoglobulin domains

hypotheses.hypothesis: High monomer mechanostability promotes superior β-sheet crystallization and alignment during fiber formation
hypotheses.result: Tetrameric constructs achieve mechanical performance matching 64-mers

model_io.model: Patient monocytes, ADA2-deficient macrophages, zebrafish model
